notable_absence.finding: The sentence 'you must set a file path for your audit logs and set the `enabled` parameter to `true`' is a genuine settings-completeness requirement (two properties of the SAME config block must both be set), but no promoted predicate cleanly expresses 'this block requires its own sub-field to be non-default' as opposed to 'this concept requires a separate setting concept' - requiresSetting's established shape (per requires-setting.json) is subject=statement/behavior, object=a DIFFERENT named setting, and applying it with the same concept on both sides is a stretch. Recorded above with an honest self-referential flag rather than silently dropped, per the instruction not to delete a relation to dodge a modelling difficulty without noting it.

cross_component_finding: This page is the direct resolution of the round's second watch-for question. audit-logging.md states only 'Viewing and managing audit logs permissions are enforced through Sync Gateway RBAC controls', without saying which of Sync Gateway's role-shaped systems it means. This page removes the ambiguity on two fronts: first, by enumerating audit logging's only configuration surfaces as 'the bootstrap config (file based config)', 'the database config using existing Admin REST API endpoints', and 'the audit-specific Admin REST API endpoint config/audit' - all Admin-REST-API-gated, none touching the sync-function/channel layer where sgw:role lives; second, and most directly, by defining 'cbs' as 'Users that are are RBAC controlled. These are created on Couchbase Server. Sync Gateway's Admin and Metrics REST APIs are authenticated using Couchbase Server users' in the same breath it defines the unrelated 'sgw' domain as 'Users and Roles that are created by and operate solely within Sync Gateway'. Since this page uses the word 'RBAC' only for the cbs/Couchbase-Server-user domain and never for sgw:role, 'Sync Gateway RBAC controls' in audit-logging.md's sentence is resolved to sgw:rbac-user, not sgw:role.
cross_product_finding: The disabled_users/disabled_roles filtering mechanism operates across BOTH of Sync Gateway's disjoint identity systems at once (a single audit config can list a cbs-domain user and an sgw-domain role side by side, as example 1's payload shows: user1/cbs disabled alongside role1/sgw disabled) - a single Sync Gateway feature whose configuration surface spans both halves of the two-layer security model this project has been tracking since round 3 (own channel/role model for data sync + reused Server RBAC for administration). No other Sync Gateway page read so far requires a single JSON payload to name principals from both domains simultaneously.
